# Independent audit: invariant buffered contact continuation

Audited in full:
`candidate c6bafe9ff5de0861`.
The requested emphasis was Sections 2, 5 and 6; Sections 3--4 were also
independently compared with the signed uniform-envelope proof in
`candidate d750a370b2e831ee`.



## Exact cover and continuity

The changing normal norm must be retained inside the weighted contact
minimum as A_i(t)=sum rho_ij Gamma_t(u_ij). Its presence makes the
weighted expression (6) precisely the sum of the CURRENT buffered
cap margins. Once the weighted quantile sum is raised by the exact
alpha_i(t), at least one margin is nonnegative at every point of every
new actual fiber in J_i. This proves the cap containment and upper
budget without guessing the new maximizing source.

The minimum is attained on a finite union of compact fibers. Old
interior contact marks remain inside all nearby bodies. A minimizing
sequence has a convergent subsequence at one fixed base; energy
continuity, including its zero boundary extension, identifies its
limit as the unique old contact. Neither nesting nor a rate for the
new minimizing mark is used.

The old own trace is proper. It supplies strict local decrease of the
tail near the old quantile, uniformly for nearby bodies; thus the
nearby RIGHT quantiles exist continuously and solve the exact common
mass equation by bracketing. Projection gaps elsewhere do not affect
this argument.

For bases outside I, joint upper semicontinuity is valid. For each
fixed nonvertical cap, volume convergence of all fiber indicators,
marked-energy continuity, and covariance continuity give cap-mass
convergence: its boundary is Lebesgue-null in every positive fiber.
Pure-base closed caps are upper semicontinuous; on a convergent actual
source sequence the finite base is eventually fixed. Taking the
infimum and then using compactness of the finitely many nondeepest
fibers preserves the strict original gap. This proves the global
comparison (8) for arbitrary compatible fixed-base Hausdorff paths.

## Uniform shape expansion

The stated bounded signed radial hypotheses are sufficient. Their
sphere-almost-everywhere limit transfers to surface-almost-everywhere
normal speeds because radial projection for a convex body containing
a fixed ball has a bounded positive radial surface Jacobian. Signed
oriented shell integration gives the uniform expansion for bounded
Lipschitz integrands.

Common interior mark balls bound the projective minimizers. Their
optimal denominator floor 1/(d+1) transfers to the old bodies with
only O(t) error, so the new parameters remain admissible on a common
compact set. Uniqueness gives uniform optimizer convergence, and
the two minimizing evaluations prove the envelope expansion. This
matches the independent proof cited above; no uncontrolled derivative
of an infimum or assumption of smooth convex boundaries is present.

## Covariance and finite-contact coefficient

If Q_z=int_(K_z)(X-g_z)(X-g_z)^T, differentiating the centroid inside
Q_z gives no terms, because int_(K_z)(X-g_z)=0. Thus dot Q_z is just
the negative boundary integral of the centered quadratic times v_z.
Differentiating Sigma=(sum Q_z)/M gives exactly

    dot Sigma=(D Sigma-J)/M.

At old Gamma(u_ij)=1 the square-root derivative is one half the
quadratic form. Since sum rho=1, the contribution of D Sigma is D,
so dot A_i=(D-J_i^cov)/(2M), with the displayed signs.

The normalized energy derivative is f_i/N[-C_z/E_i+D/M]. Applying
the finite contact minimum to A_i(t)f_t therefore gives

    dot alpha_i=epsilon f_i[min_z C_z/(N E_i)
                               -D/(N M)-dot A_i].

The minimum remains over all original contact bases. The alternative
coefficient -(N+2)D/(2NM) in (17) is correct after substituting dot A_i.
The signed case permits either sign for dot alpha; the exact cover
does not need it nonnegative.

## Actual response and scope

The regular quantile expansion implies

    dot q_i=-sum theta_ij L_ij-dot alpha_i/B_i.

Dividing by the SAME actual M_t produces (19), with the additional
beta D term and no missing mass normalization. All speed functionals
are evaluated on the same physical path. Finite strict inequalities
for every group imply genuine normalized buffered-depth descent by
the exact global comparison, without a deepest-point path.

The source correctly leaves the existence of such a paying path
unproved. Its supporting-facet response scope is also explicit:
regular expansion (11) is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence
of Hausdorff continuity or a declaration that supporting contacts
are proper.

As a useful exact normalization check, take three identical intervals
[-R,R] at bases -1,0,1. At their unique buffered deepest point, the
invariant buffer gives physical shift epsilon R/3 and

    Q_epsilon=R(3+epsilon/3),   M=6R.

For R=1-h t, old Gamma-normalized u have magnitude sqrt(3). Hence
D=6h, J_i^cov=18h, dot A_i=-h; the normalized energy buffer at the
contact stays 1/sqrt(3), so dot alpha_i=epsilon h/sqrt(3).
Each fixed old cap loses 3h, B_i=sqrt(3), and the covering loss is
3h+epsilon h/3, exactly beta D. The normalized quantity is constant,
as affine invariance requires. Omitting either the covariance term
or the total-mass term would destroy this identity.
